subject: Literature
title: Translation and Poetry Across Languages
description: A micro-lesson that makes Translation and Poetry Across Languages usable.

hook.text: Robert Frost said poetry is what gets lost in translation, but translators have been proving him wrong for centuries.

buildup.text: Translated poetry connects cultures: Rumi, Neruda, and Szymborska are read worldwide because translators carried them.

discovery.text: Great translators do not just convert words but recreate the poem's music, rhythm, and feeling in a new language.

twist.text: Some translations become masterpieces in their own right, like Fitzgerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam in English.

climax.text: Translation ensures that poetry remains humanity's shared inheritance, not the property of any single language.

punchline.text: Every translated poem is a bridge between two worlds.

quiz.question: What do great poetry translators actually do?
options: They convert words one-to-one between languages
They recreate the poem's music, rhythm, and feeling in a new language
They simplify the original to make it easier to understand
